key_concepts: Copy Previous Pass Output to Input
common_gotchas: GLSL Advanced POP is the correct choice when a shader needs to change output counts or write multiple point/vertex/primitive classes; keep Max Points and max primitive capacities large enough for the intended output.
I[] index buffer writes are only available for Advanced POP primitive outputs when the relevant Max Primitives mode is custom or otherwise allocates writable topology capacity.
Extra Outputs are named shader namespaces and are selected downstream with GLSL Select POP; keep extra-output names stable because generated helper names include them.
Per Primitive Batch dispatch is useful when all primitives in the current batch have the same type, but batch helper functions should be used instead of assuming global primitive or vertex indices.
When changing point, vertex, or primitive counts, do not assume every input attribute still has a one-to-one output element; explicitly write or initialize the attributes the branch needs.
Use Init Output Attributes, Copy Previous Pass Output, or explicit writes for every allocated attribute before downstream reads; uninitialized SSBO data can lead to unstable geometry.
Line-strip outputs need consistent Line Strip Info, line-strip index-per-vertex data, max verts per line strip, and primitive restart handling.
Use Topology POP when multiple Advanced POP passes each produce part of the final topology and combining/declaring topology outside shader code is clearer.
When Delete Input Attributes is enabled, only explicitly output attributes remain available downstream.
Inspect Info CHOP/operator errors for compile errors, warnings, and cook health before treating empty output as a topology-only issue.
